significance: A sea temple on the Perancak estuary in Jembrana marking the place where the priest Dang Hyang Nirartha is held to have come ashore in Bali in 1546. Once sited on a hilltop and known as Tanjung Ketapang, it was moved to the marshland side and rebuilt twice as a dang kahyangan temple, anchoring the Hindu community in a largely Muslim district.
story: The name is traced to ancak, meaning split: when the village head I Gusti Ngurah challenged Nirartha, the stone seat beneath him is said to have cracked apart.
